descripcion_es: Clauses with -ing, having + past participle and the past participle: Having finished…, Built in 1900…
resumen: Participle clauses condense a subordinate clause (of time, reason or a relative clause) into a verb form with no subject. They are typical of written and formal English, and the implied subject must be the same as the subject of the main clause.

filas: simultaneous action or reason, active meaning
Feeling tired, I went to bed early.
Having finished the report, she went home.
Built in 1900, the station is now a museum.
Having been warned, we took umbrellas.
After leaving school, he joined the army. When asked, she refused.

explicacion.texto: Golden rule: the implied subject of the participle is the subject of the main clause. Walking home, the rain started (wrong: it seems that the rain is walking). Walking home, I got caught in the rain (right).
They can also replace defining relative clauses: The man sitting next to me (= who was sitting). The products made in this factory (= which are made).

items: Negation: not before the participle: Not knowing the way, we asked a local.
Having + past participle makes it clear that the action happened earlier: Having seen the film, I didn't want to read the book.
Active meaning → -ing; passive meaning → past participle.

ejemplos.frase: Opening the drawer, she found an old photograph.
ejemplos.traduccion: Al abrir el cajón, encontró una foto antigua.

ejemplos.frase: Having lived in Berlin for years, he speaks fluent German.
ejemplos.traduccion: Como ha vivido en Berlín muchos años, habla alemán con fluidez.

ejemplos.frase: Written in simple language, the guide is easy to follow.
ejemplos.traduccion: Escrita en un lenguaje sencillo, la guía es fácil de seguir.

ejemplos.frase: Not wanting to wake the baby, they whispered.
ejemplos.traduccion: Como no querían despertar al bebé, hablaban en susurros.

ejemplos.frase: The woman talking to the director is my aunt.
ejemplos.traduccion: La mujer que está hablando con el director es mi tía.

ejemplos.frase: Asked about the merger, the CEO declined to comment.
ejemplos.traduccion: Al preguntarle por la fusión, el consejero delegado declinó hacer comentarios.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Arriving at the hotel, the receptionist gave us the keys.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Arriving at the hotel, we were given the keys by the receptionist.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The implied subject (we arrived) must be the same as the subject of the main clause.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Built the house in 1990, it needs repairs.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Built in 1990, the house needs repairs.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: A past participle clause does not take an object: it has a passive meaning.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Having not seen the email, I missed the meeting.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Not having seen the email, I missed the meeting.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Not usually goes at the beginning of the participle clause.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct participle form.
ejercicios.frase: ___ (finish) his homework, Leo went out to play.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the row “Having + past participle: earlier action, active meaning”. The clue is that he first finished his homework and then went out: the action happened earlier, and Leo is the one who performs it (active meaning). Also, the implied subject is the same as in the main clause, Leo, as the golden rule requires. The form is Having + finished.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Earlier action with active meaning: having + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Después de terminar los deberes, Leo salió a jugar.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Finishing
errores_previstos.explicacion: The simple -ing form suggests simultaneity; to make the earlier action clear, this unit uses having + past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Finished
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past participle only has a passive meaning; Leo finished his homework, so the meaning is active.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Having finish
errores_previstos.explicacion: After having, the past participle finished is needed, not the infinitive.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct participle form.
ejercicios.frase: ___ (paint) by Goya, the portrait is worth millions.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the row “Past participle: passive meaning”. The clue is “by Goya”: the portrait does not paint, it was painted by Goya, and by introduces the agent of a passive. The implied subject is the portrait, the same as in the main clause. The form is the past participle Painted, equivalent to “which was painted”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Pintado por Goya, el retrato vale millones.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Painting
errores_previstos.explicacion: The -ing form has an active meaning: it would say that the portrait paints. With by + agent, the past participle is needed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Having painted
errores_previstos.explicacion: Having + past participle is active and earlier: the subject (the portrait) would be the one who painted.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Paint
errores_previstos.explicacion: A participle form is needed; the infinitive cannot start the sentence with this function.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct participle form.
ejercicios.frase: ___ (not / know) what to say, she simply smiled.
ejercicios.explicacion: Two rules from this unit apply: -ing expresses a reason with active meaning, and in the negative not goes before the participle (“Not knowing the way, we asked a local”). The clue is the cause-and-effect relation: she smiled because she did not know what to say. The implied subject is she, the same as in the main clause. The form is Not knowing.
ejercicios.traduccion: Como no sabía qué decir, se limitó a sonreír.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Knowing not
errores_previstos.explicacion: Not goes before the participle, not after it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Don't knowing
errores_previstos.explicacion: Participle clauses do not use the auxiliary do; the negative is just not in front.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Not known
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past participle has a passive meaning (“not being known”); she is the one who does not know, so -ing is needed.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct participle form.
ejercicios.frase: The people ___ (wait) outside have been there for hours.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit explains that these forms can also replace defining relative clauses: “The man sitting next to me” is equivalent to “who was sitting”. The clue is that the people are performing the action of waiting (active meaning) at that moment. That is why the form is waiting, equivalent to “who are waiting”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: It replaces an active relative clause (who are waiting): -ing.
ejercicios.traduccion: La gente que está esperando fuera lleva horas ahí.

errores_previstos.respuesta: waited
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past participle gives a passive meaning (“the people who are waited for”); the people are the ones waiting.

errores_previstos.respuesta: who waiting
errores_previstos.explicacion: It mixes the relative clause and the reduced form: either “who are waiting” or just “waiting”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: are waiting
errores_previstos.explicacion: Without who, the sentence would have two finite verbs; the reduced form is just waiting.

ejercicios.frase: ___ twice, he decided not to apply again.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the row “Having been + past participle: earlier action, passive meaning”. The clue is that he did not reject anyone: he was rejected, and that happened before he made the decision. That is why both having (earlier action) and been + past participle (passive) are needed. The implied subject, he, is the same as in the main clause.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Earlier and passive action (he was rejected): having been + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Como lo habían rechazado dos veces, decidió no volver a presentarse.

por_opcion.Having been rejected: Correct. It expresses a passive, earlier action: first he was rejected and then he decided.
por_opcion.Having rejected: Incorrect. It is active: it would say that he rejected something, the opposite of the meaning of the sentence.
por_opcion.Rejecting: Incorrect. It is active and simultaneous: it would say that he was rejecting something while deciding.

ejercicios.frase: Most of the cars ___ in this factory are exported.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit explains that the past participle replaces a passive relative clause: “The products made in this factory” is equivalent to “which are made”. The clue is that the cars do not make anything: they are made in the factory. That is why the form is made, the past participle of make.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Passive meaning (which are made): past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: La mayoría de los coches fabricados en esta fábrica se exportan.

por_opcion.made: Correct. Made has a passive meaning and is equivalent to “which are made”.
por_opcion.making: Incorrect. Making is active: it would say that the cars make something.
por_opcion.having made: Incorrect. Having made is active and earlier; it is not used to reduce relative clauses of this kind either.

ejercicios.frase: ___ along the beach, we saw a group of dolphins.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the row “-ing: simultaneous action or reason, active meaning”. The clue is that walking and seeing the dolphins happen at the same time, and we are the ones walking. The implied subject, we, is the same as in the main clause. That is why the form is Walking.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mientras paseábamos por la playa, vimos un grupo de delfines.

por_opcion.Walking: Correct. The -ing form expresses an active action simultaneous with the main one.
por_opcion.Walked: Incorrect. The past participle has a passive meaning, which makes no sense with walk here.
por_opcion.Having walked: Incorrect. It would mean that the walk ended before they saw the dolphins, when in fact they saw them while walking.

ejercicios.frase: Locating in the city centre, the hotel is perfect for tourists.
respuestas: Located in the city centre, the hotel is perfect for tourists.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the rule “Active meaning → -ing; passive meaning → past participle”. The clue is the hotel: it does not locate anything, it is situated (is located) in the centre. That is why the correction is Located, the past participle. Locating would mean that the hotel finds or places something.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The hotel “is situated”: passive meaning, past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Situado en el centro de la ciudad, el hotel es perfecto para los turistas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Locating in the city centre, the hotel is perfect for tourists.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: the meaning is passive and needs located.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Being locating in the city centre, the hotel is perfect for tourists.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It still uses -ing with active meaning; the passive form is located (or being located).

errores_previstos.respuesta: Located at the city centre, the hotel is perfect for tourists.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The participle is correct, but we say in the city centre.

ejercicios.frase: Having not received an answer, I wrote again.
respuestas: Not having received an answer, I wrote again.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit says that in the negative not goes before the participle and that the usual form is “Not having seen the email”. The clue is “Having not received”. The correction is “Not having received an answer”. Note that “having not” sometimes appears in real use, but the recommended and more natural form is not having.
ejercicios.traduccion: Como no había recibido respuesta, volví a escribir.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Having not received an answer, I wrote again.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: this unit puts not before having.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Not having receive an answer, I wrote again.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The position of not is correct, but after having the past participle received is needed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Don't having received an answer, I wrote again.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Participle clauses do not use do; the negative is just not.

ejercicios.frase: The children played in the park are my nephews.
respuestas: The children playing in the park are my nephews.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit explains that defining relative clauses can be reduced: with active meaning, -ing is used (the man sitting next to me). The clue is that the children are the ones playing: it is an active relative clause, “who are playing”. The past participle played would give a passive meaning, and the sentence would also seem to have two main verbs. The correction is playing.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Reduced active relative clause (who are playing): -ing, not the past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los niños que están jugando en el parque son mis sobrinos.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The children played in the park are my nephews.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: the meaning is active and needs playing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The children who playing in the park are my nephews.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It mixes the relative clause and the reduced form: “who are playing” or just “playing”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The children are playing in the park are my nephews.
errores_previstos.explicacion: There are two unconnected finite verbs; the reduced form drops the auxiliary: playing.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite with a participle clause starting with Having.
ejercicios.frase: After she had read the contract, she signed it.
respuestas: Having read the contract, she signed it.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the row “Having + past participle: earlier action, active meaning”. The clue is the past perfect “had read”: reading happened before signing. When the clause is reduced, the conjunction after and the subject she disappear, because she is the same as the subject of the main clause. Read has a past participle spelt the same as the infinitive, although it is pronounced /red/.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Earlier active action: having + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Después de leer el contrato, lo firmó.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Having readed the contract, she signed it.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Read is irregular: its past participle is read, not readed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Having she read the contract, she signed it.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The participle clause has no subject of its own: she is removed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Having read the contract, signed it.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The main clause needs its subject: she signed it.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite with a past participle clause at the beginning.
ejercicios.frase: The castle, which was destroyed in the war, was rebuilt in 1960.
respuestas: Destroyed in the war, the castle was rebuilt in 1960.
ejercicios.explicacion: This unit explains that the past participle replaces a passive relative clause. The clue is “which was destroyed”: the castle was destroyed, a passive meaning. When the clause is reduced, the participle Destroyed moves to the beginning, which and was are removed, and the subject the castle, which is the same, stays in the main clause.
ejercicios.traduccion: Destruido durante la guerra, el castillo se reconstruyó en 1960.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Destroying in the war, the castle was rebuilt in 1960.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The -ing form has an active meaning: it would say that the castle was destroying something.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Having destroyed in the war, the castle was rebuilt in 1960.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Having + past participle is active; an earlier passive action would need having been destroyed, and the instructions ask for a past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Destroyed in the war, it was rebuilt in 1960.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It replaces the castle with it although there is no antecedent; the subject of the main clause must be kept.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite with an -ing clause at the beginning.
ejercicios.frase: Because he felt ill, Mark stayed at home.
respuestas: Feeling ill, Mark stayed at home.
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the row “-ing: simultaneous action or reason, active meaning”. The clue is “Because he felt ill”, a reason simultaneous with the main action. When the clause is reduced, because and he disappear, and felt becomes Feeling. The implied subject is Mark, the same as in the main clause.
ejercicios.traduccion: Como se encontraba mal, Mark se quedó en casa.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Felt ill, Mark stayed at home.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past participle has a passive meaning; Mark is the one who feels ill: Feeling.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Because feeling ill, Mark stayed at home.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Because is not used before a participle clause; the reason is implied in the -ing form.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Feeling ill, he stayed at home Mark.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject of the main clause is Mark and it goes before the verb; he is not added.

respuestas: having missed the bus I walked
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the row “Having + past participle: earlier action, active meaning”. First the bus was missed and then the person walked, and the same person (I) does both things. The order is the participle clause (having missed the bus) and then the main clause with its subject (I walked).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Having + past participle expresses the earlier action.
ejercicios.traduccion: Como había perdido el autobús, fui andando.

errores_previstos.respuesta: having the bus missed I walked
errores_previstos.explicacion: The participle missed goes right after having, before the object: having missed the bus.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I having missed the bus walked
errores_previstos.explicacion: The participle clause has no subject in front; I is the subject of walked and goes with the main clause.

respuestas: when asked he refused to comment
he refused to comment when asked
he refused when asked to comment
ejercicios.explicacion: This uses the row “Conjunction + -ing / past participle: makes the relation clear”, with the example “When asked, she refused”. The clue is that he was asked (passive meaning), so the past participle asked is used after when, equivalent to “when he was asked”. The reduced clause can go at the beginning or at the end, which is why both orders are accepted. Refuse to comment means “decline to make any comment”. He refused when asked to comment is also correct, where to comment depends on asked (“when they asked him to comment, he refused”).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Conjunction + past participle (when he was asked).
ejercicios.traduccion: Cuando se lo preguntaron, se negó a hacer comentarios.

errores_previstos.respuesta: when he asked refused to comment
errores_previstos.explicacion: Putting he before asked makes the clause active (“when he asked”), and the main clause is also left without a subject.

errores_previstos.respuesta: when he refused asked to comment
errores_previstos.explicacion: It breaks up the two clauses: when must go with asked (when asked), and refused with its subject he and its complement to comment.

descripcion_larga_es: Participle clauses condense a subordinate clause of time, reason or a relative clause into a verb form with no subject: Feeling tired, I went to bed; Built in 1900, the station is now a museum. They are typical of written and formal English and make reports and essays more concise. Spanish speakers find it hard to choose between -ing, the past participle and having + past participle, and to respect the rule that the implied subject must be the subject of the main clause.

contexto.que_es: They are reduced subordinate clauses that use a participle form instead of a finite verb with its subject and conjunction. The -ing participle expresses active meaning and simultaneity or reason; the past participle, passive meaning; having + past participle, an earlier active action; and having been + past participle, an earlier passive action. They can also replace relative clauses: the man sitting next to me.
contexto.por_que_importa: They let you write in a more compact and elegant way, which is highly valued in B2 and C1 essays and in professional reports. Used wrongly, they produce striking mistakes: if the implied subject is not the same as the subject of the main clause (dangling participle), the sentence says something absurd, such as that the rain was walking home.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: They appear in written texts, news and descriptions: to link actions (Having finished the report, she went home), explain reasons (Not knowing the way, we asked) or describe things (Located in the city centre, the hotel…). Spanish speakers tend to use -ing where a passive meaning is needed, to put not in the wrong place and to forget that the subject must be the same.
